title: fix(scripts): refuse a verification claim on a doc fragment the gate never compiles
body:
Fixes #7505

## What changed

`check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` now refuses **one combination**: a `declared`
fragment whose written reason claims the block *was checked* against something.

A `declared` fragment is the single block this gate never compiles. A reason
asserting the block agrees with a shipped artifact is therefore an assertion the
gate structurally cannot re-verify — it goes silently false the day the thing it
names changes, and a reader cannot tell the two apart because both arrive in the
same marker.

⭐ The exemption is **not** the defect and is untouched. Exempting a fragment
from compilation stays legitimate; a verification claim stays legitimate on a
block the gate actually compiles. Only the two together are refused, and the
author has two ways out, both named in the failure text: say why the block
cannot compile without asserting it was checked, or move the block into the
compiled tier where the claim becomes one this gate re-verifies on every commit.

⛔ No exemption list. An exemption here would be a second unverifiable assertion
about an unverifiable assertion.

## The census, which is what chose the route

The card asked for this before any gate change, and it decided the shape:

| | |
|:--|:--|
| declared fragments in the corpus | **158** |
| carrying a verification claim | **2** |
| where | both on `content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx`, the page the card sampled |
| how they were spelled | `verified` · `hand-checked` |

⇒ The card's stated precondition for this route — *"needs the marker vocabulary
to be enumerable; if 'checked against' is free prose, this becomes a phrase hunt
with false positives"* — **tests positive**. The vocabulary is a closed list, and
the check reads only the marker's reason field (a small structured field this
gate already validates for length), never the page's prose.

Two corpus reasons deliberately stay legal, and both are pinned as tests:

- `plugin-calendar.mdx` names the same authority to say the **opposite** — its
  block *"cannot compile against the SHIPPED prop type"*. Anchoring the match on
  "against the shipped" would have flagged it; anchoring on a **verb** does not.
- `component-registry.md` says its literal is *"type-checked on the complete
  example at the end of the page, which does compile"*. `type-check` names this
  gate's own action, so that is a claim backed by a check that re-runs every
  commit — the shape the rule wants, not the shape it refuses.

⚠️ Stated limit, in the header too: this matches verbs, it does not parse
meaning. `type-checked by hand` would pass it. It closes the spelling that has
actually been written here and turns a silent gap into a red build on the commit
that reintroduces it.

## Ablation — the proof, not "I added a check and CI is green"

The falsified marker's own historical wording, put back on the same `declared`
fragment. Mutation proven on disk before the run; restoration proven by state.

```
HEAD blob        : ab9e86d56a1c369052cefd9e86c3e2d31d504d9a
PRE  : claim=0 anchor=2
POST : claim=1 anchor=1          <- anchor-count flip, so the edit landed
mutated hash     : c704938b04d381b4a7dc5bfe4fe3311688200396

GATE EXIT (mutated) = 1          <- ran and found errors
  content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx:117  [verification-claim-on-fragment]
  a DECLARED fragment is never compiled, so this gate cannot re-verify "Checked"
  on any later commit ...

RESTORED: claim=0 anchor=2
restored hash    : ab9e86d56a1c369052cefd9e86c3e2d31d504d9a
hash == HEAD blob: YES
git diff HEAD    : empty (clean)
GATE EXIT (restored) = 0         findings after restore: 0
```

The gate names itself in the finding (`[verification-claim-on-fragment]`) and
leaves through exit **1** — a verdict about the document — not exit 2, which
would say it never judged anything. A test pins that distinction.

## The page repair that ships with it

`content/docs/utilities/data-objectstack.mdx`, read against **today's shipped**
`packages/data-objectstack/dist/index.d.ts` rather than against the card's text.
Two things, not one:

1. Both marker reasons rewritten to state the gap instead of claiming a check.
2. ⚠️ **A second falsehood, found by doing exactly that reading.** The card's
   named defect — the return type — was already repaired on `main` by #7503, so
   that premise arrived stale. But the config excerpt was still missing a member
   the shipped declaration carries: `systemCapabilities?: string[]` (ADR-0066).
   Added, with the shipped doc comment's own wording. The marker's old claim that
   *"every config member declared there with the same type"* had been checked was
   false again, in a second way, at the moment it was read.

⇒ That is the card's thesis reproducing itself inside its own sampling point.

## Tests

`scripts/__tests__/check-doc-snippet-types.test.ts`: **70 → 78 passing.**

The 8 new pins cover the refusal *and its edges*, because a suite that only
proved "the claim turns it red" would not notice the check growing into a phrase
hunt: the measured spelling turns red and names itself · it is a document verdict
not a precondition · the same words on a **compiled** block are untouched · a
reason naming the same authority to say the opposite stays legal · `type-checked`
stays legal while `hand-checked` still trips · every verb in the closed list
trips it, so the list cannot rot in silence · this repository's own 158 declared
fragments carry no claim (guarded against going vacuous) · the header states the
rule so it cannot drift out of the source.

## Gates run, all at `e16a473a8`

| gate | exit |
|:--|:--|
| `check:doc-snippets` (this gate) | 0 |
| `check:doc-types` · `check:doc-fences` · `docs:check-links` · `check:doc-example-readers` | 0 |
| doc-gate vitest suites (snippet + component + fence), 156 tests | 0 |
| `type-check:scripts` | 0 |
| `lint:root` (the scope that covers `scripts/`), full run | 0 errors |
| `lint:coverage` · `type-check:coverage` | 0 |
| `check-control-bytes` | 0 |

`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` verdict, verbatim:

> ✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this
> range, so no changeset is owed.

⇒ No changeset added, and ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label applied — in this repo
that label is read by nothing and exempts nothing; the gate's verdict line is the
authority.

**Not run:** the full `turbo run lint` / `turbo run type-check` package fan-out
(no package source changed — the root scope is what covers `scripts/`); any
browser or runtime verification (nothing here runs in a browser); CI itself.

## Scope

Exactly the three files the dispatch named. `UNGATED_DOCS` is **byte-identical**
to `HEAD` — verified, not assumed — so there is no collision with #7417, which is
editing that ledger's `README.md` entry. The scan population is unchanged at 158
declared fragments and 456 compiled blocks, confirming this did not quietly move
any fragment into the compiled tier.
